package_info.package_manager: source (Linux distribution package, upstream open source project)
package_info.why_malicious: The XZ package was compromised by a backdoor inserted by an attacker who gained commit access through social engineering. The malicious code allowed unauthorized remote access by subverting cryptographic operations in the affected versions.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when SSH authentication is performed using liblzma)
execution_context.file_location: liblzma code (injected into the build system and source files of xz)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Obfuscated code in liblzma that hooks into the SSH authentication process, allowing a crafted SSH key to trigger remote code execution.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Intercepts SSH authentication requests and, when a specially crafted key is presented, allows the attacker to execute arbitrary code or bypass authentication.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is obfuscated, not documented, and is not part of the legitimate compression functionality of xz/liblzma. It interacts with SSH authentication, which is outside the expected scope.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: liblzma should only provide compression/decompression functionality, not interact with authentication or network processes.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; compression libraries should not interact with authentication mechanisms.
key_indicators: Code paths triggered by specific SSH key patterns

execution_context.file_location: m4/build system scripts and test files

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious m4 macros and test files that inject the backdoor code into the build output, only under certain conditions.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Ensures the malicious code is only included in certain builds, making detection harder and targeting specific distributions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Build scripts are modified to conditionally inject code, which is not standard practice and is designed to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Build scripts should not contain logic to inject hidden or obfuscated code into binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Conditional compilation is legitimate, but not for injecting hidden backdoors.
key_indicators: Conditional code injection in build scripts
Test files with dual purpose (testing and payload delivery)

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains trust and commit access to the xz project via social engineering.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to modify source code and build scripts

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is inserted into build scripts and source files, obfuscated to avoid detection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Backdoor code is included in distributed binaries

attack_chain.action: Backdoor code in liblzma is triggered at runtime when SSH authentication occurs with a crafted key.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains unauthorized remote access or code execution

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated or undocumented code in compression libraries
Unexpected hooks into authentication or network processes
Conditional code injection in build scripts
file_indicators: Modified m4 macros or test files in xz source
network_indicators: Connections or authentication attempts using crafted SSH keys
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected or obfuscated code in compression libraries, especially those that interact with authentication or network processes. Review build scripts for conditional code injection or unexplained logic. Analyze SSH authentication logs for anomalies, such as successful logins with unusual keys or patterns. Compare distributed binaries with upstream source to detect unauthorized modifications.
